title: TIA Recognition and Secondary Stroke Prevention Principles
subject: Medicine
preview: TIA is transient focal neurological dysfunction from ischemia without evidence of acute infarction in the modern tissue-based concept.
quickRevision: TIA is transient focal neurological dysfunction from ischemia without evidence of acute infarction in the modern tissue-based concept.
Neurovascular imaging, cardiac rhythm evaluation and vascular risk management inform secondary prevention.
Differentials include migraine aura, seizure and metabolic mimics.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: TIA is transient focal neurological dysfunction from ischemia without evidence of acute infarction in the modern tissue-based concept.
Even resolved symptoms may warn of early stroke risk, requiring urgent evaluation.

sections.title: Differentiate and manage
points: Neurovascular imaging, cardiac rhythm evaluation and vascular risk management inform secondary prevention.
Differentials include migraine aura, seizure and metabolic mimics.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not discharge a resolved unilateral weakness episode as harmless solely because the examination is now normal.

quiz.question: Why does a resolved focal neurological episode still require urgent assessment?
options: It may signal a high early stroke risk
quiz.explanation: It may signal a high early stroke risk. Even resolved symptoms may warn of early stroke risk, requiring urgent evaluation.
